title: Care without a running account
meaning: Your shared home needs fair participation that does not turn care into a constant audit of mutual debts.
text: Domestic support grows here through tangible care: groceries bought, dinner made and a room made more comfortable. The Empress in the physical position of Muladhara describes sustaining daily life through these actions. Justice in energy tests the routine through excessively precise accounting: you want assurance that each effort receives an equal response. Strength in emotions helps you contain irritation and handle it gently. Yet a calm outward reaction does not necessarily mean the question of who now owes what has stopped sounding within.

Imagine cooking together in the evening. As you chop vegetables, yesterday’s cleaning, the grocery shopping and an extra trip to the shop all come to mind. Each of you has an invisible list. **A shared task is easier when care is noticed before a bill is presented.** You can acknowledge that someone has done more today and still finish dinner peacefully. Every gesture need not receive immediate compensation to remain part of a fair household.

The difficulty is mistaking restraint for settled agreement. An unspoken tally accumulates, and gentleness begins to require increasing effort. An unwashed cup then provokes irritation stretching back over several days. You try to protect balance and quietly lose the pleasure of caring for each other. Fairness stays responsive when it includes what both of you can currently manage, alongside the number of jobs completed.
